statement.text: Conjecture Let $G$ be an abelian group of odd order and let $A,B \subseteq G$ satisfy $|A| = |B| = k$. Then the elements of $A$ and $B$ may be ordered $A = \{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B = \{b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$ so that the sums $a_1+b_1, a_2+b_2 \ldots, a_k + b_k$ are pairwise distinct.

title: Snevily's conjecture
